w:r.w:t: Finance work fails when it relies on memory or on any one person holding the whole process. This playbook replaces that with structure: defined systems, separated duties, bounded authorities and a predictable calendar — so the numbers are accurate, the controls hold, and nothing compliance-critical is ever a surprise.

4.1 · Service standards — what great looks like
The standards that keep it all consistent — service standards, the delegations register, recurring payments, accounting policy, the audit program, and how this document is controlled.
Qualitative standards across the whole function — not targets, but how the work should always feel to the Board and everyone it touches.
Figures are right the first time and reconcile to Xero. Every number is supported and audit-ready without a scramble.
Pay runs, remittances and lodgements land on or before the date — the calendar is worked ahead, never caught up to.
Separation of duties and delegations hold every time. Controls are never traded away for speed or convenience.
Payroll, banking and personal data are held in absolute confidence; security is instinctive (see 1.6).
Work follows Philippine Accounting Standards and statutory obligation — correct, not just convenient.
Plain, helpful communication with staff, suppliers and the Board. Firm on controls, warm in manner. Always Be Kind.
The Board trusts the numbers without re-checking them, the auditor finds no surprises, and no statutory date is ever missed. Trust in the books is the measure of the function.

A plain-language summary of the policies that govern the books. The authoritative wording lives in the Finance Operations Manual; these are the working essentials.
General-purpose statements under Philippine Accounting Standards, on the accrual basis and historical cost — modified where applicable by fair value.
Revenue, expenses and assets are net of VAT except where not recoverable from the BIR. Net VAT due to/from the BIR sits in payables/receivables.
Carried at cost (or fair value) less depreciation. Equipment under the capitalisation threshold (~$1,000) is expensed and held on an asset inventory listing.
Straight-line over useful life from the date ready for use; rates, residuals and useful lives reviewed each reporting period.
Receivables reviewed for collectability; uncollectible debts written off when identified. Trade payables unsecured and normally paid within 30 days.
Benefits provided for as services are rendered. Finance leases capitalised; operating-lease payments expensed over the term.
Current vs non-current is judged on the 12-month operating cycle. Figures rounded to the nearest dollar; the chart of accounts changes only with the GM’s approval.
Controls are tested on a fixed schedule, in a spirit of collaboration and improvement. Findings are tracked to closure in Asana and reported to the Board.
